arcs.title: Dana and the basil cups
arcs.stage: 3/5 going to 4/5 — tonight after havdalah she comes to see Moshe at the apartment (her Nov 5 promise was never verified from the log). Next: a first date.

arcs.title: Saving Moshe
arcs.stage: 1/3 going to 2/3 — tonight Dana diagnoses him: too much afternoon sun on the sill and plucking the wrong leaves. New spot, new rules.

arcs.title: Gadi and the chickpea logo
arcs.stage: Due Sunday morning. Tonight, after havdalah, Gadi texts; Ishai finally writes a fee number in his reply and sends it.

arcs.title: Noa, the best friend
arcs.stage: Shabbat dinner Fri Nov 6 was planned (not verified). Today she stays offstage; next week she wants a report on Dana.

arcs.title: Falafel the dog
arcs.stage: Settled in. Today a long Shabbat walk; Mr. Zelig decides Falafel is a better listener than the pigeons.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Lesson 1 planned Nov 5 (not verified). Tonight he uses 'yes, and' for real: he names his fee to Gadi. Next: lesson 2, Thu Nov 12.

beats.goal: A slow Shabbat morning at home: no phone, no laptop. Ishai has coffee by the window, looks at Moshe's dry leaves and starts tidying the apartment for tonight, when Dana comes to see the basil after havdalah. He talks to Falafel and Moshe.
beats.forceText: Ishai stands by the window with coffee, looking at Moshe, then picks a sock up off the floor.

forceLines.say: Tonight you have a doctor, Moshe. Try to look alive.

forceCommentary.say: He's cleaning for a plant visit. Moshe never got this treatment.

moments.text: Shabbat morning light. Ishai, in an old T-shirt, holds a mug of coffee by the window and studies Moshe's brown-edged leaves. Falafel stretches on the rug.

lines.say: Tonight you have a doctor, Moshe. Try to look alive.

commentary.say: A doctor. He means the cute barista. We all know he means the cute barista.
Moshe looks like he read the reviews of his own life.

moments.text: He puts the mug down and starts a slow tidy: a sock off the floor, cushions straightened, three cups carried to the sink. He stops and looks around the room like a stranger would.

lines.say: Does it look like a person lives here, or like a person gave up?

commentary.say: Three cups by one couch. That's not a home, that's a crime scene.

beats.goal: A long Shabbat walk with Falafel in the park. Mr. Zelig is on his bench talking to the pigeons. He wants a new listener and adopts Falafel as one. Ishai, who never says no, ends up hearing about tonight from the old man's odd angle: Zelig guesses there is a woman, because a man doesn't walk a dog this slowly unless he is thinking.
beats.forceText: On the park bench Mr. Zelig talks to Falafel while the pigeons wait for crumbs.

forceLines.say: The dog listens. The pigeons only want bread.

forceCommentary.say: Zelig found a new audience. The pigeons are filing a complaint.

moments.text: Quiet Shabbat park, joggers and pigeons. Mr. Zelig sits on his bench throwing crumbs and lecturing the birds. Falafel pulls Ishai straight to him and sits at the old man's feet.

lines.say: Finally. Someone who listens. The pigeons only want bread.
Shabbat shalom, Mr. Zelig. He'll listen to anyone with crumbs.
So he's honest. Better than most people on this bench.
You're the only one on this bench.
Exactly. Sit. You walk slow today. A man walks slow when he's thinking.
I'm just walking the dog.
The dog wants to run. You want to think. Who is she?
There's no she. Someone's coming to look at my basil.
Ha. In 1971 a girl came to look at my tomatoes. Forty years married.
It's really about the basil.

commentary.say: Forty years from one tomato visit. Moshe, no pressure.
The pigeon guy has better radar than me. I'm furious.

moments.text: Ishai sits at the other end of the bench. Mr. Zelig hands him a piece of bread for the pigeons and keeps one for Falafel, who takes it very gently.

lines.say: Advice. When she comes, don't talk too much about the plant.
She's coming for the plant. What else would I talk about?
Ask her one question that isn't about leaves. One. Then shut up.
What question?
If I knew questions, would I be talking to pigeons?
Fair.
Leave me the dog. Take the pigeons. Fair trade.
No deal, Mr. Zelig. But thank you. Really.
Thank me at the wedding. Go, go, he's bored of you.

commentary.say: One question that isn't about leaves. Write it on your hand, Ishai.
He offered pigeons for a dog. Best business deal on this show.

update.memory: Ishai walks a brown dog called Falafel, listens patiently. Someone is coming to see his basil; Zelig told him to ask her one non-plant question.

beats.goal: Ishai takes Falafel out on Herzl Street in the quiet Shabbat afternoon. Tomer, loud as ever, walks by from his parents' lunch with a container of leftovers and stops. He hears about Dana tonight and wants to help in all the wrong ways; then he spots the flickering hallway light through the building door and promises to fix it after Shabbat, because Ishai never asks.
beats.forceText: Tomer stops Ishai on the quiet Shabbat street, a container of his mother's leftovers under one arm.

forceLines.say: Ishai! My mother made too much. Take it, you look hungry.

forceCommentary.say: Every mother in this city is feeding Ishai. He's a national project.

moments.text: Herzl Street is empty and quiet, Avi's kiosk shut. Tomer comes down the sidewalk with a plastic container under his arm and sees Ishai with Falafel from far away.

lines.say: Ishai! On Shabbat, outside, in daylight! Who are you?
Tomer, it's a quiet street. People are sleeping.
So I'm the alarm clock. My mother made too much. Meatballs. Take.
Thank you. Tell her thank you.
You're cleaner than usual. You shaved. What's going on?
Someone's coming tonight to look at my basil.
Someone. A woman someone? I'll come. I'll be the cool friend.
You will absolutely not come.
Okay, okay. Light candles. Women love candles.
It's after Shabbat, Tomer. The candles are the havdalah one. It's a plant visit.

commentary.say: Tomer as the cool friend. I'd pay for that disaster.
Meatballs for the basil date. The mothers have a plan.

moments.text: Tomer looks past him through the glass of the building door, where the hallway light flickers on and off.

lines.say: That light. How long is it doing that?
A month? Two? I stopped seeing it.
You have an electrician friend since first grade and you don't ask?
I didn't want to bother you.
Bother me! That's what I'm for. Tomorrow evening, I come with the ladder.
Okay. Yes. Thank you. Tomorrow.
See? Yes. Easy. And tonight, ask her something not about the plant.
Why does everybody say that?
Because we know you. Bye, Falafel! Bye, Romeo!

commentary.say: He said yes to help without saying sorry. Yael, take a bow.
Two months of flickering. Ishai is a man who adapts to anything.

update.memory: Ishai has someone coming to see his basil tonight. Tomer gave him his mother's meatballs and will fix the flickering hallway light Sunday evening.

beats.goal: Shabbat is out. Ishai does a simple havdalah at home (wine, spices, the braided candle), then takes his phone out of the drawer. A text from Gadi is waiting about Sunday morning. This time, with Noa's push and Yael's homework in his head, he answers with an actual fee number and sends it before he can change his mind. Then he panics a little, and Dana is due soon.
beats.forceText: After havdalah Ishai takes his phone out of the drawer, reads a text from Gadi and types a reply with a number in it.

forceLines.say: Four thousand five hundred. Send. Don't think. Sent.

forceCommentary.say: He sent a number! A real number! I need to sit down.

moments.text: Three stars outside. Ishai lights the braided havdalah candle, says the blessing over a little wine, smells the spice box and holds it to Falafel's nose, then puts the flame out in the wine.

lines.say: Shavua tov, you two. Good week.

commentary.say: He let the dog smell the spices. Falafel is now officially Jewish.
Shabbat ends. The phone comes out of the drawer. The week begins to hurt.

moments.text: He takes the phone out of the drawer. A text from Gadi is already waiting. He sits at the desk, types, deletes, types again, and stares at the number on the screen.

message.say: Shavua tov! Chickpea for 9am tomorrow? Client's very excited. Just make it friendly. Thanks!!

lines.say: Nine. Friendly. Excited. And not one word about money.
My fee for the friendly version is four thousand five hundred. Send. Sent.

commentary.say: He sent a number! A real number, with zeros! I need a minute.
Gadi used two exclamation marks. That's how you know he's scared too.

moments.text: He puts the phone face down, picks it up, puts it down again. Then he sees the time, grabs the last cups off the table and moves Moshe's pot to the center of the sill.

lines.say: Okay. Business, done. Moshe, stand up straight. She's coming in half an hour.

commentary.say: He asked for money and invited a woman over on the same night. Who is this man?

beats.goal: Dana keeps her promise and comes to see Moshe after Shabbat. Deadpan as always, she treats it as a real house call: Moshe gets too much hot afternoon sun on the sill and Ishai has been pinching the wrong leaves. She moves the pot and shows him how to pinch the tops. Ishai remembers Zelig's and Tomer's advice and asks her one question that isn't about plants. It is shy and real, not a date yet; she leaves by about 21:30 with something left open.
beats.forceText: Dana crouches by the windowsill, turning Moshe's pot in her hands while Ishai hovers beside her.

forceLines.say: He's not dying. He's sunburned. And you've been pinching the wrong leaves.

forceCommentary.say: She's in his apartment. Dana is in the apartment. Everybody stay calm.

moments.text: A knock. Dana stands at the door in a dark jacket, hands in her pockets, no smile. Falafel rushes her; she crouches and lets him sniff her hand before she looks up at Ishai.

lines.say: Shavua tov. I'm here for the patient.
Shavua tov. Come in. This is Falafel, he's not the patient.
Falafel. You named a dog after a sandwich.
He was found next to a falafel kiosk. It was that or Tahini.
Good choice. Tahini's a cat name.
Do you want something? Water? Tea? Meatballs? Long story.
Patient first. Where is he?
On the windowsill. Be gentle, he's had a hard month.
I'm a barista. I'm always gentle. With plants.

commentary.say: With plants! She clarified! There's a whole novel in that pause!
He offered meatballs. To a woman. On a first visit. Bold.

moments.text: At the windowsill Dana turns Moshe's pot slowly, rubs a dry leaf between her fingers, pushes a finger into the soil. Ishai stands too close, then a step too far.

lines.say: He's not dying. He's sunburned. This window cooks him every afternoon.
I put him there so he'd be happy.
Everyone thinks more sun is love. It's not. Morning light, that's it.
And the dry leaves? I've been pulling them off.
Those are fine. You pinch the tops, here, above two new leaves.
Like that? I'm scared I'll hurt him.
You'll hurt him less than the window. Pinch. Good. Now he grows wider.
Wider is good?
For basil, yes. For people, it depends.

commentary.say: Moshe has a diagnosis. Sunburn. I've been saying it for a week.
She held his hand to pinch a leaf. I'm calling it. Contact!

moments.text: Moshe now sits on the small table near the other window. Ishai and Dana have mint tea at the table, Falafel asleep on her foot. He holds his cup with both hands and gathers himself.

lines.say: Can I ask you something that isn't about leaves?
That's suspicious. Go.
Why the basil on my cups? You don't draw on anyone else's.
You noticed that.
I'm a designer. I notice things. I just don't say them.
The first time, you talked to your cup. You told it to have a nice day.
I did not.
You did. So I thought the cup should have something to say back.
That is the nicest thing a barista has ever said to me.
Don't get used to it. I'm on early shift tomorrow.

commentary.say: He asked the question! One question, not about leaves! Zelig, you genius!
He talks to cups. She draws on them. They're perfect and it's terrible.

moments.text: At the door to the corridor Dana zips her jacket. The hallway light flickers over them both. She looks up at it, then at him.

lines.say: Your light's broken.
My friend's fixing it tomorrow. I asked. I'm asking for things now.
Good. Keep doing that.
Thank you for coming. For Moshe. Really.
Morning light. Pinch the tops. Text me in a week with a picture.
I don't have your number.
Give me your phone. There. Now you have a reason. Good night, Ishai.
Good night, Dana. Shavua tov.

commentary.say: She put her number in his phone herself. Season one, we did it.
A photo of Moshe in a week. The basil is now a matchmaker. I'm so proud.

update.memory: Visited Ishai's apartment to treat Moshe (sunburn, wrong pinching). He asked why she draws basil on his cups. She gave him her number; wants a Moshe photo in a week.

hosts: Shabbat morning. The city is so quiet you can hear Moshe being dramatic.
No laptop today. The chickpea is sitting alone in the dark, thinking about friendliness.
He is tidying. Ishai is tidying. Mark the date.
Rule of this apartment: the phone sleeps in a drawer on Shabbat. Gadi sleeps nowhere.
Falafel has spent Shabbat lying in exactly the patch of sun Moshe needs.
Tonight is the house call. I've been ready since Thursday.
Oren, are you nervous for Moshe? Be honest. Your hands are shaking.
A basil with a doctor's appointment. This is the most important night of his life.
Herzl Street on Shabbat: one cat, two pigeons, zero buses.
The kiosk is closed. Avi is somewhere, resting, dreaming of tahini.
He shaved. On Shabbat afternoon. For a plant.
If you see Ishai fluff a cushion, no you didn't.
Moshe's leaves are crispy. Like the falafel he's named after. Wait, no, that's the dog.
Slow walk, slow coffee, slow everything. Shabbat suits him.
Somewhere, Noa is texting him and the drawer is getting all of it.
Three stars and the week starts. I'm counting stars for him.
Havdalah smells like cloves and the end of the weekend.
Sunday morning is the chickpea deadline. Saturday night is Dana. Choose your fighter.
He's going to talk about plants for an hour. I can feel it.
One question that isn't about leaves. That's the whole mission.
Moshe has been moved. Moshe has been moved before. Moshe is tired.
He talks to the dog like a colleague. Falafel takes it well.
Nothing happened for ten minutes and I loved every one of them.
Rest day. Even the hosts deserve one. We don't get one.
A quiet Shabbat apartment is just a man, a dog and a basil, listening to the fridge.
Tomorrow there's a lecture at eleven. Tonight there's mint tea. Priorities.
radio: Shavua tov from Radio Herzl 88.2. The week is back, put your shoes on.
Saturday night in the city: buses waking up, kiosks opening, everybody hungry at once.
If you spent Shabbat on the couch, congratulations, you did it right.
Next up, something slow for the people still in their socks.
A listener asks: is it too late to start the week over? It's Saturday night. You haven't started.
Sunday tomorrow. Set the alarm now, before you forget who you are.
Somebody on Herzl Street just ordered three falafels. We're not judging. We're jealous.
Radio Herzl, keeping your kitchen company since your kitchen was lonely.
Plants, dogs, dates. Whatever you're nervous about tonight, it's a good song for it.
The night is cool and dry. Bring a jacket, bring a friend, bring snacks.
Weekend's over in three, two... no, wait, we've got one more song.
To everybody hosting tonight: the cups don't need to match. Nobody looks at the cups.

zelig: On Shabbat even the pigeons are lazy.

michal: Saturday is legs. Saturday is always legs.
Nobody's here. The mirror is all mine.
sivan: Twelve kilometers or I don't go home.
Saturday night treadmill. Don't tell anyone.
Why is the gym empty? Oh. Right.
lior: She opens the door and... no. She doesn't open the door.
What if the basil is a symbol?
kobi: I almost won once. Nineteen ninety eight. Almost.

chat.say: Shavua tov to everybody. Who left a bicycle on the second floor? It's not a parking.
Sorry, mine. Moving it now. Shavua tov!
Reminder: the hallway light is flickering again. Somebody's friend is an electrician?
Does anyone have a spare charger? Mine died over Shabbat.
I heard a woman on the stairs. Just saying. Shavua tov.
Recycling day tomorrow. Bottles out tonight please, not at 6 am.
